source_metadata.exact_title: SkillZip: Contract-Preserving Graph Compression for Scalable Agent Skill Libraries

validated_atoms.canonical_statement: The study asks how a skill provider can retrieve and expose the smallest sufficient executable procedural context under a limited context budget.
SkillZip is proposed to unify retrieval, compression, execution, and maintenance around source-grounded contract-bearing section subgraphs rather than whole skill packages.
A section node is represented with an execution role, content, input and output signatures, resources, guards or verifier conditions, and a source pointer.
SkillZip uses nine operational section roles: Intent, Trigger, Input, Precondition, Operation, Resource, Failure, Verifier, and Output.
The procedural contract is separated into interface, execution, and verification aspects, while source pointers retain provenance for reversible expansion.
Sec2Graph segments skill packages using headings, lists, code blocks, warnings, argument descriptions, tool references, and tests, with model-assisted boundary refinement when cues are incomplete.
Sec2Graph links operations to inputs, preconditions, resources, verifiers, and repair handlers and selects an intent or trigger root plus a verified output terminal for each skill subgraph.
Cross-skill reuse is exposed by linking occurrence-specific sections to a shared canonical prototype only when role, boundary signature, resource, and verifier behavior are compatible.
MotifZip grows motif candidates only within compatible typed signatures and counts support over non-conflicting occurrence-specific source subgraphs rather than over canonical prototypes.
MotifZip accepts a macro only when its interface is stable, dependencies are closed or exposed through ports, and state-changing operations retain reachable verification.
Accepted MotifZip macros are reversible graph-grammar rewrites that store occurrence mappings, typed ports, executable contracts, verifier hooks, source pointers, and rendering levels.
MotifZip scores contract-valid motifs with a local description-length gain that rewards frequency and cross-skill reuse while penalizing boundary cuts and execution risk.
MotifZip uses a conflict-aware greedy rewrite policy and does not claim global optimality over all overlapping motifs.

For pairwise non-conflicting accepted occurrences, macro rewriting followed by source expansion recovers the typed external dependencies and operation-to-verifier reachability of the recorded source subgraph up to auxiliary prototype links.
The lifting guarantee is structural rather than semantic and does not establish equivalence of unrecorded behavior or correctness of the verifier itself.
PathHydrate converts a query into a structured task object containing the goal, expected outputs, required capabilities, visible inputs, domain or executor profile, and ordered subgoals.
PathHydrate fuses section-level dense matching with skill-level rankings using reciprocal-rank fusion to improve section precision without losing package-level coherence.
PathHydrate compiles a compact connected subgraph subject to anchor coverage, dependency closure, verifier reachability, and a procedural-content budget.

PathHydrate repairs selected operations by recovering required Input, Precondition, Resource, Failure, Verifier, and Output sections and falls back to the smallest skill-level bundle when no verifier-reachable context fits the budget.

Selected macros are rendered at the lowest sufficient hydration level among name, contract, outline, and full source, with expansion triggered when required inputs, guards, verifiers, or source pointers are not exposed.

ReZip assimilates new skills by reusing compatible existing macros, buffering unmatched residual subgraphs, and promoting residual motifs only after repeated cross-skill support, positive compression gain, and contract validation.
ReZip tracks macro uses, source expansions, verifier failures, and downstream repair cost; macros exceeding a risk threshold are first hydrated in more detail and may later be split or retired.
The default SkillsBench evaluation uses all 87 benchmark tasks under a 1,000-skill library setting.
The ALFWorld evaluation uses all 140 episodes from the valid_seen split.
SkillsBench task reward is the percentage of deterministic verifier tests passed after artifact execution.

outcome.definition: Percentage of deterministic verifier tests passed.

validated_atoms.canonical_statement: ALFWorld task reward is the percentage of episodes that reach the goal within the common step and attempt budgets.

outcome.definition: Percentage of episodes reaching the goal within common execution budgets.

validated_atoms.canonical_statement: The default experimental setting uses SkillsBench with a 1,000-skill library, MiniMax-M2.7, and a 3,000-token procedural-content selection budget; the default ALFWorld budget is 1,200 tokens.
All task-analysis, retrieval-control, and action-generation calls use temperature 0 and deterministic decoding when supported.

Repeated-run statistical experiments use five matched runs paired by task or episode and random seed, with confidence intervals from paired outcome-level bootstrap differences and significance from paired permutation tests.
Local structural-construction timings exclude LLM extraction and start from cached section records; the reported server uses an Intel Xeon Gold 6248R CPU with 512 GB memory.
With MiniMax-M2.7 on SkillsBench, SkillZip achieved 33.3% reward versus 27.3% for SkillDAG, a 6.0-point improvement.

quantitative_result.effect_measure: absolute difference in reward, percentage points

validated_atoms.canonical_statement: With MiniMax-M2.7 on ALFWorld, SkillZip achieved 79.3% success versus 67.1% for SkillDAG, a 12.2-point improvement.

quantitative_result.effect_measure: absolute difference in success rate, percentage points

validated_atoms.canonical_statement: With gpt-5.2-codex on SkillsBench, SkillZip achieved 43.0% reward versus 36.8% for SkillDAG, a 6.2-point improvement.

quantitative_result.effect_measure: absolute difference in reward, percentage points

validated_atoms.canonical_statement: With gpt-5.2-codex on ALFWorld, SkillZip achieved 96.4% success versus 93.6% for SkillDAG, a 2.8-point improvement.

quantitative_result.effect_measure: absolute difference in success rate, percentage points

validated_atoms.canonical_statement: On SkillsBench with MiniMax-M2.7, SkillZip increased Ret@1 from 66.7% with SkillDAG to 73.6%.

quantitative_result.effect_measure: absolute difference in Ret@1, percentage points

validated_atoms.canonical_statement: On ALFWorld with MiniMax-M2.7, SkillZip increased Ret@1 from 57.9% with SkillDAG to 85.7%.

quantitative_result.effect_measure: absolute difference in Ret@1, percentage points

validated_atoms.canonical_statement: On SkillsBench, SkillZip achieved a 3.46× compression ratio while retaining 99.2% dependency preservation.
On SkillsBench, SkillZip retained 98.7% verifier reachability at a 3.46× compression ratio.
Text compression matched SkillZip at 3.46× compression but reduced dependency preservation to 65.0% and verifier reachability to 60.0%.

quantitative_result.effect_measure: dependency preservation rate under text compression

validated_atoms.canonical_statement: Text compression required recovery for 45.0% of queries versus 14.8% for SkillZip and achieved 25.5% reward versus 33.3% for SkillZip.

quantitative_result.effect_measure: absolute difference in reward, percentage points

validated_atoms.canonical_statement: Replacing section-level nodes with skill-level nodes reduced reward from 33.3% to 27.9% and Ret@1 from 73.6% to 66.7%.

quantitative_result.effect_measure: absolute difference in reward, percentage points

validated_atoms.canonical_statement: Removing dependency-closure checks reduced dependency preservation from 99.2% to 82.3% and reward from 33.3% to 28.6%.
Removing verifier constraints reduced verifier reachability from 98.7% to 76.4% and reward from 33.3% to 29.1%.
Disabling adaptive hydration increased rendered context from 1,941 to 2,587 tokens while reward decreased from 33.3% to 31.5%.

SkillZip reduced active storage from 18.6 MB for the raw section graph to 5.4 MB while retaining the 112.4 MB source library for reversible expansion, corresponding to a 71.0% active-storage reduction.
Removing SkillZip contract checks reduced active storage only from 5.4 MB to 4.9 MB but increased fallback from 7.2% to 24.7% and downstream inflation from 2.7% to 23.4%.
Contract extraction achieved a macro-average field-level F1 of 91.6% and exact match of 84.6% against human annotations.
Source-pointer extraction reached 96.2% F1 and 93.5% exact match, while precondition and guard extraction reached 88.7% F1 and 79.6% exact match.
With 10% synthetic contract corruption, reward was 31.6%, dependency preservation 96.8%, and verifier reachability 95.1%.
With 40% synthetic contract corruption, reward fell to 24.1%, verifier reachability to 77.2%, macro expansion rose to 41.3%, and full-source fallback rose to 34.7%.
As the candidate library grew from 200 to 100K skills, SkillDAG Ret@1 fell from 72.1% to 41.8%, whereas SkillZip Ret@1 fell from 78.3% to 65.1%.

population.label: Fixed SkillsBench evaluation queries across scaled candidate libraries

validated_atoms.canonical_statement: At 100K skills, similar-skill confusion was 12.4% for SkillZip versus 48.2% for SkillDAG.

population.label: Fixed SkillsBench evaluation queries with 100K candidate skills

quantitative_result.effect_measure: absolute difference in confusion rate, percentage points

validated_atoms.canonical_statement: At 100K skills, SkillZip had a 4.29× compression ratio and 248.3 ms online retrieval-and-hydration latency per query.
Increasing controlled procedural overlap from low to high increased mean macro support from 2.3 to 9.7 occurrences and compression ratio from 1.18× to 4.63×.

Across low, medium, and high procedural-overlap conditions, dependency preservation stayed at or above 99.1%, verifier reachability stayed at or above 98.8%, and reward varied only from 32.4% to 33.5%.
In the data-wrangling domain, SkillZip achieved 36.4% reward versus 29.7% for SkillDAG with a 4.21× compression ratio.

population.label: Data-wrangling partition of the 1,000 SkillsBench skills

quantitative_result.effect_measure: absolute difference in reward, percentage points

validated_atoms.canonical_statement: Across the reported procedural domains, verifier reachability ranged from 98.5% to 99.4%.

quantitative_result.effect_measure: minimum verifier reachability across reported domains

validated_atoms.canonical_statement: Increasing the SkillsBench procedural-content budget from 1,000 to 2,000 tokens raised reward from 22.4% to 31.5%; reward was 33.3% at 3,000 tokens and 34.1% at 5,000 tokens.
Under the default 3,000-token selection budget, SkillZip rendered 1,941 tokens per task on average and 1,947 tokens at the median.
SkillZip reduced mean rendered context by 72.1% versus top-5 whole-skill loading (1,941 versus 6,958 tokens) and by 88.8% versus top-12 whole-skill loading (17,384 tokens).

quantitative_result.effect_measure: percent reduction versus top-5 whole-skill loading

validated_atoms.canonical_statement: Under the default budget, 51.7% of tasks rendered fewer than 2,000 tokens and 74.7% rendered fewer than 2,500 tokens; the 1,000–1,500 token interval was the modal bin at 26.4% of tasks.

concept.text: Share of tasks below 2,000 rendered tokens

validated_atoms.canonical_statement: Local graph construction plus MotifZip took 1.44 seconds for 1,000 skills and 178 seconds for 100K skills using cached section records.
At task time, SkillZip required 27.9 ms for local retrieval and rendering versus 41.2 ms for SkillDAG, while rendering 1,941 versus 3,103 tokens.

concept.text: Local online retrieval and rendering latency

validated_atoms.canonical_statement: Compared with SkillDAG, SkillZip reduced total trajectory prompt processing from 2,782,696 to 1,473,532 tokens, a 47.0% reduction.

concept.text: Total prompt tokens across agent trajectory

quantitative_result.effect_measure: percent reduction in total prompt tokens

validated_atoms.canonical_statement: Compared with SkillDAG, SkillZip reduced completion tokens from 31,963 to 20,601, a 35.5% reduction.
Compared with SkillDAG, SkillZip reduced average tool calls from 36.9 to 28.9, a 21.7% reduction.
Compared with SkillDAG, SkillZip reduced average task time from 429.7 to 339.0 seconds, a 21.1% reduction.

After ten arriving-skill batches with injected contract drift, ReZip achieved 3.64× compression, 33.2% reward, and 98.6% verifier reachability at 0.22× the cumulative update cost of periodic full recompression.
The static compressed graph degraded to 28.7% reward and 91.2% verifier reachability after the streaming updates and contract drift.
ReZip responded to injected contract drift within 1.4 batches on average, compared with 1.0 batch for full recompression.

concept.text: Mean batches to recover from contract drift

validated_atoms.canonical_statement: Across five matched runs on SkillsBench with MiniMax-M2.7, SkillZip improved reward over SkillDAG by 6.0 points (95% CI 3.8 to 8.1; p=0.004).
Across five matched runs on ALFWorld with MiniMax-M2.7, SkillZip improved success over SkillDAG by 12.2 points (95% CI 7.5 to 16.8; p<0.001).
Across five matched runs on SkillsBench with gpt-5.2-codex, SkillZip improved reward over SkillDAG by 6.2 points (95% CI 4.4 to 8.0; p=0.002).
Across five matched runs on ALFWorld with gpt-5.2-codex, SkillZip improved success over SkillDAG by 2.8 points (95% CI 0.4 to 5.2; p=0.031).
On SkillsBench with Claude Sonnet 4.5, SkillZip achieved 52.4% reward versus 26.2% with Vector Skills.

quantitative_result.effect_measure: absolute difference in reward, percentage points

validated_atoms.canonical_statement: On SkillsBench with Gemini 3 Pro, SkillZip achieved 44.4% reward versus 19.3% with Vector Skills.

quantitative_result.effect_measure: absolute difference in reward, percentage points

validated_atoms.canonical_statement: On ALFWorld, SkillZip reached 97.9% success with Kimi K2.5, 99.0% with Claude Sonnet 4.5, and 99.1% with Gemini 3 Pro.

quantitative_result.effect_measure: maximum reported SkillZip ALFWorld success among listed backbones

validated_atoms.canonical_statement: In failure attribution, stages controlled by SkillZip accounted for 58% of remaining failures: retrieval 26%, contract extraction 18%, and hydration 14%.

population.label: Failed or repaired default SkillsBench trajectories

quantitative_result.effect_measure: failure share attributed to SkillZip stages

validated_atoms.canonical_statement: Downstream executor and system stages accounted for 42% of remaining failures, including 33% from agent execution and 9% from infrastructure.

population.label: Failed or repaired default SkillsBench trajectories

quantitative_result.effect_measure: failure share attributed to executor/system stages

validated_atoms.canonical_statement: The case studies are illustrative constructions based on recurring benchmark patterns rather than additional quantitative samples.
Fresh LLM-assisted contract-extraction wall-clock time is provider dependent and is not extrapolated to the 100K-skill setting; large-scale structural timings start from cached section records.
End-to-end task wall time includes provider and container variation and is treated as systems evidence rather than an isolated retrieval-speed measurement.
The authors conclude that retrieving execution-complete sections provides more useful procedural context than treating skills as indivisible packages.
The authors conclude that contract-preserving compression is valuable because shorter context alone does not guarantee executable context.
The authors conclude that SkillZip improves skill-library scalability while maintaining executable structure and supporting efficient, reliable reuse in long-horizon agent tasks.

extraction_limitations: Extraction is source-grounded to the uploaded arXiv v1 preprint and was not externally verified.

Atoms prioritize independently reviewable study objectives, methods, benchmark definitions, quantitative findings, explicit limitations, and author conclusions; references and general background claims were not atomized exhaustively.
Quantitative context uses the paper's reported benchmark populations and metric definitions; no missing sample sizes or study details were invented.
Calculated or normalized structures are distinguished by assertion_origin; the canonical statements are concise normalizations of source claims rather than verbatim quotations.
The paper states that its structural lifting guarantee is not a proof of semantic equivalence or verifier correctness.
The paper states that its case studies are illustrative constructions rather than additional quantitative samples.
No funding, conflict-of-interest, or data-availability atom was created because a corresponding disclosure was not identified in the accessible source text.
